validation.notes: Arduino Nano ESP32 is one PCB (u-blox NORA-W106-10B, ESP32-S3, 16 MB GD25B128 flash, 8 MB PSRAM, USB-C) sold as two SKUs: ABX00092 without headers and ABX00083 with headers. The ABX00083 user manual covers both ('with and without headers'), so they are one catalog record with both SKUs as aka, never two ids. Not to be confused with Nano 33 IoT / Nano RP2040 Connect, whose u-blox NINA-W102 (ESP32) is only a radio co-processor.

The PAM lead is Freenove's starter kit; the one board it ships is the Freenove ESP32-WROVER board (kit FNK0060, repo Freenove_ESP32_WROVER_Board 'Apply to FNK0060'). Freenove's FNK0060 Preface describes it: built on the PCB-antenna ESP32-WROVER module, CH340 for code download, camera interface, reset and boot buttons. Two board revisions share the product (the earlier one is no longer mass-produced); both are this one record. Siblings kept distinct: the Freenove ESP32-WROOM board (repo Freenove_ESP32_WROOM_Board, 'Apply to FNK0090') and the Freenove ESP32-S3-WROOM board are different boards and must not be authored here.

Espressif's user guide lists six ordering codes: ESP32-S2-DevKitM-1-N4R2 (ESP32-S2-MINI-2, 4 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM, PCB antenna), ESP32-S2-DevKitM-1 (EOL, ESP32-S2-MINI-1, 4 MB, no PSRAM, PCB antenna), ESP32-S2-DevKitM-1R (EOL, MINI-1, 4 MB, 2 MB PSRAM, PCB antenna), and the -1U/-1U-N4R2/-1RU counterparts with an external antenna connector (MINI-1U/MINI-2U). The record covers the PCB-antenna DevKitM-1 board; the U (external antenna) SKUs stay distinct and must not be authored under this id. PSRAM differs between PCB-antenna variants (0 or 2 MB), so psram_mb is omitted. Distinct from catalogued esp32-s2-devkitc-1 (SOLO/WROOM module, 8 MB flash) and esp32-s2-saola-1.

validation.notes: LILYGO's product page (T-Beam SUPREME: ESP32-S3FN8, 8MB flash, 8MB PSRAM, QMI8658 IMU; variants L76K or UBLOX GNSS x 433/868/915/920 MHz and L76K 144~148 MHz) and its official LoRa-Series hardware doc (ESP32-S3FN8, SX1262 or LR1121 radio, L76K or u-blox M10 GNSS, SH1106 OLED, AXP2101 PMU with an 18650 holder, USB-C) describe one board. The GNSS and frequency/radio options, including the 144~148 MHz SX1278 build LILYGO documents on its own hardware page, are variants of this one product listing and stay in this one record (as the catalogued T-Beam does with its region SKUs); no per-variant record may appear. Kept distinct: the original ESP32 T-Beam (already catalogued as lilygo-t-beam, unchanged), the T-Beam-BPF and the T-Beam-1W (separate LILYGO boards).

Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V4 (model HTIT-WB32LAF): ESP32-S3R2 (2MB PSRAM) + external 16MB flash + SX1262, CP2102 removed (native USB). The product page now sells a sibling WiFi LoRa 32 V4-R8 (ESP32-S3R8, 8MB PSRAM, different firmware and Vext/VGNSS/LED pin map) which is a distinct SKU and must not be authored by this work. The predecessor WiFi LoRa 32 V3 (ESP32-S3FN8, CP2102) is already catalogued as heltec-wifi-lora-32-v3 and stays separate. The low-power HTIT-WB32LAF-N-HF/-LF/-433 radio variants (21 dBm) are the same board with a different LoRa front end and are covered in notes, not as separate ids.

ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board (Espressif, now listed under EOL boards; hardware v1.5.2 documented, v1.4 older revision of the same product) carries a pre-v3 ESP32-P4 plus an ESP32-C6-MINI-1 radio module. The successor ESP32-P4X-Function-EV-Board (chip revision v3.x), the ESP32-P4X-C5-Function-EV-Board (ESP32-C5 radio) and the ESP32-P4-EYE / ESP32-P4X-EYE camera boards are distinct products with their own user guides and must not be merged into this id. v1.4 differs from v1.5.2 by a CP2102N USB-to-UART port instead of native USB Serial/JTAG and by IO24/IO25 on the header.

SparkFun's product page (SKU WRL-24408) and its hookup guide describe one board: ESP32-S3-MINI-1-N4R2 (4MB flash, 2MB PSRAM) on the Thing Plus (Feather) footprint, USB-C wired straight to the ESP32-S3's native USB (schematic: D+/D- to IO20/IO19, no bridge chip), MCP73831 charger + MAX17048 fuel gauge, Qwiic, microSD on SDIO, WS2812 on IO46, 21 header GPIOs. Kept distinct: the ESP32 WROOM and ESP32-S2 WROOM Thing Plus boards (already catalogued as sparkfun-thing-plus-esp32-wroom and sparkfun-thing-plus-esp32-s2-wroom, unchanged), and the ESP32-C6 / ESP32-C5 Thing Plus boards SparkFun lists in the same family (different SoCs; no record for them may appear). The product page's 2.55in length and 'WiFi 6' line contradict the hookup guide and official dimension drawing (2.30in x 0.90in) and the ESP32-S3 silicon; they are not used.
